featured.title: BloodLink
featured.lead: Finding an eligible donor during a medical emergency is a search problem with a clock attached. BloodLink turns it into a ranked, auditable pipeline.
featured.body: A full JavaFX desktop system that takes an emergency blood request and walks it end to end — eligibility assessment, ranked donor matching, request lifecycle, in-app notification, and an audit trail that survives the incident.
highlights: Role-based authentication across donor, requester and administrator
Eligibility engine — donation intervals, availability state and blood-group compatibility
Ranked donor matching with candidate scoring, not a flat list
Full request lifecycle with status history and audit entries
Achievement badge tiers to keep donors returning
Administrator dashboard with demand analytics
89 source files, unit-tested, nine architecture documents

featured.title: Ishuchats
featured.lead: The easy version of a chat app polls a database. This one doesn't. Messages are pushed the moment they exist.
featured.body: A multi-user private messaging application where the network layer and the storage layer have separate jobs and never confuse them. Sockets carry delivery; MySQL only remembers.
highlights: Hand-written packet protocol over Java TCP sockets, documented in PROTOCOL.md
Push delivery — the client never polls the database for new messages
Handshake, private routing and live online/offline presence
BCrypt password hashing, non-modular build to avoid FXML reflection traps
Text and image messages with persistent history
Bundled dark and light themes

featured.title: FSM Cache Controller
featured.lead: A cache controller is a state machine before it is ever silicon. This one is written as exactly that — and then made to run.
featured.body: A direct-mapped, write-back cache modelled as an explicit finite state machine and driven by a CPU request trace. Written in pure Python with no dependencies so the logic has nowhere to hide.
highlights: Four explicit states — IDLE, COMPARETAG, ALLOCATE, WRITEBACK
Direct-mapped cache, four lines, write-back with dirty-bit eviction
256-entry main memory with a four-cycle access penalty
Reads a CPU trace of read and write requests from file
Zero external dependencies — standard library only
Built with a team of three

featured.title: Earthquake Management System
featured.lead: A country that sits on a fault line should be able to model what happens after the shaking stops.
featured.body: A C++ object-oriented system for coordinating earthquake response — modelling incidents, resources and the relationships between them through inheritance and polymorphism rather than a pile of structs.
highlights: Class hierarchy modelling incidents, zones and response resources
Inheritance and polymorphism used as the organising principle
Encapsulated state with controlled interfaces
Collaborative build
